item.description:
Sport · Aichi-Nagoya 2026

Asian Games October 3: Korea football, Lee Woo-seok and Song Da-bin take gold

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-10-05 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

South Korea beat Japan 1–0 in the men’s football final with EOM Jisung’s second-half goal. Lee Woo-seok and Song Da-bin also won gold, while Oh Ye-jin and Hongten took silver. These matches were played on October 3; the source article was published on October 5.

Coverage: five selected South Korean finals on October 3.

Official records were checked on October 5, 2026, at 12:48 KST. The three gold and two silver results below are not South Korea’s full daily medal tally. This is a record-based report, not eyewitness coverage or a live broadcast.

Selected finals

Scores list the Korean entrant first. Identical-looking numbers represent different scoring systems.

Men’s football: EOM Jisung scores at 61′

The gold-medal match began at 19:30 at Toyota Stadium. The official record shows EOM Jisung, 61′, with a 0–0 first half and 1–0 second half. Duration is listed as 90:00. The 1–0 result is the match goal score, not a penalty shoot-out. The China–Uzbekistan bronze match was a separate event.

The real Toyota Stadium photograph shows a J.League match in 2010, not this goal, these spectators or the 2026 final.

Recurve archery: gold and shoot-off silver

Lee Woo-seok won the 14:50 men’s final against Japan’s Junya Nakanishi, 6–2 in set points. His points by set were 2, 1, 1, 2: wins in the first and fourth, draws in the middle. Six is not the total arrow score.

In the 10:50 women’s final, Oh Ye-jin faced India’s MOHOD Kumkum Anil. Regular-set points were 2, 1, 0, 2, 0 versus 0, 1, 2, 0, 2, totaling 5–5. Oh’s shoot-off arrow scored 8; the opponent’s X scored ten. The deciding set point gave the opponent a final 6, leaving Oh with silver at 5–6.

The final 5–6 alone hides the tied regular match. Read Score, Set Pts and SO separately in the detailed record.

Taekwondo: Song Da-bin wins women’s +67kg

Song defeated China’s MU Wenzhe 2–1 in the gold-medal match beginning at 17:10 at Toyohashi Gymnasium. The record marks Song Gold, MU Silver and the match Official. The result is not a football-like single-point margin, and it does not provide a count of successful techniques or a success rate.

Breaking: Hongten takes silver

Hongten (KIM Hongyul) lost the B-Boys final 0–3 to Japan’s Shigekix (NAKARAI Shigeyuki) at Aichi Sky Expo Hall F, beginning at 17:06. Losing this final still means a Silver medal, not leaving without one. The breaking result should not be interpreted as LoL game wins or recurve set points.

Kim Je-deok, Kim Woo-jin and Lee Woo-seok defeated India 5–1 in set points. Arrow scores were 56–56, 57–50 and 56–54. The drawn opening set gave each side one point; the next two wins gave South Korea two each.

Kang Chae-young, Lee Yun-ji and Oh Ye-jin took silver after a 3–5 loss to India. Arrow scores were 54–54, 56–56, 51–55 and 54–54. South Korea’s set points were 1, 1, 0, 1, while India’s were 1, 1, 2, 1. Three of four sets were drawn; the third set supplied India’s decisive two points.

Mixed pairs shoot four arrows per set for a maximum of 40, while three-person teams shoot six for a maximum of 60; comparing 39 and 56 as the same scale would be misleading.

Start with the size you carry and the storage you need, not the most expensive model. In the South Korean price snapshot below, Pro 512GB costs KRW 100,000 more than Pro Max 256GB: the trade-off is storage versus a larger screen.

The product information was checked on Apple’s South Korean pages on September 26, 2026. Prices are Korean-won list prices, not US or worldwide offers, and exclude discounts, trade-in, service plans and optional coverage. Recheck before purchasing. If the battery is the only problem, compare official inspection and repair quotes with replacement cost. If one app or AI feature motivates the purchase, verify current region, language, subscription and app requirements; promised future support is not a feature available today. Fix the budget ceiling and required storage, then test handling and screen needs. item.title: 256GB or 512GB iPhone? Plan capacity from your actual usage
item.description:
Buying decisions · Storage

256GB or 512GB iPhone? Plan capacity from your actual usage

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-09-26 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Photo counts alone cannot choose a capacity. Record what you use now, what remains after normal cleanup and what temporarily peaks during travel or filming. Separate device space from cloud space.

Record current usage before deleting anything

Apple’s guidance uses Settings → General → iPhone Storage. Record actual usage and the largest categories, not the advertised capacity. If you already delete files every week to stay within a small phone, current usage may understate the material you want to keep. Keep files in the plan until you have verified any backup and decided they will not move to the new device.

Estimate growth from comparable observations

The following is an illustrative usage log, not a measured record from a tested phone.

Hypothetical usage log: 120GB → 126GB in 30 days
RecordStartAfter 30 days
Total used120GB126GB
ContextNormal photo and app storageNote travel, filming or bulk deletion
Net increase126 − 120 = 6GB / 30 days

30-day equivalent growth = (ending usage − starting usage) ÷ elapsed days × 30

The example gives 6GB. A rise from 120GB to 129GB in 45 days also gives (129 − 120) ÷ 45 × 30 = 6GB. This is a comparison basis, not a prediction that every month will be identical. Log bulk deletion, cloud optimization, cache and system changes. For a falling trend, this calculator accepts 0 growth rather than negative inputs; review temporary needs separately.

Use four planning components

Planned capacity = current usage + (monthly net growth × months of use) + temporary storage + reserve

The reserve is your planning allowance for updates, apps and unexpected capture, not an Apple-recommended percentage. Avoid adding current system usage repeatedly if it is already in the observed total, but do not assume the new device’s system use will be identical.

Hypothetical examples · GB
ExampleCalculationPlanInterpretation
A: mainly streaming90 + 1 × 24 + 20 + 30164Investigate 256GB, accounting for usable space
B: growing video library160 + 4 × 24 + 30 + 40326Compare more capacity or another storage approach
C: travel-video peak100 + 2 × 24 + 80 + 40268A peak can exceed what normal usage suggests

A plan below advertised capacity does not prove it will fit. For another hypothetical case, 120 + 6 × 36 + 30 + 40 = 406GB; changing monthly growth to 2GB produces 262GB. Both exceed the 256GB label, and 406GB does not certify that a particular 512GB device is sufficient.

The personal-use calculator is available in the original article. The formula and hypothetical examples remain in this feed.

Cloud storage does not enlarge the phone

iCloud storage and device storage are different. Synchronization and optimization can affect local use, but purchasing cloud capacity does not increase the phone’s internal capacity. Apps, offline maps and originals needed on a flight or abroad still require local space. Review synchronized deletion before assuming a cloud item can be removed safely.

Compare capacity and subscription costs without treating them as identical

Hypothetical cost example: an extra-capacity device costs KRW 300,000 more, while an imagined cloud subscription costs KRW 5,000 per month. Thirty-six months totals KRW 180,000. The apparent KRW 120,000 saving is relevant only if the two choices meet your actual needs. This is not a current iCloud price quote. A larger phone may still need a cloud subscription for another purpose.

Check sensitivity before purchasing

Without reserve, 120 + (2 × 36) + 30 = 222GB, but changing the assumed growth to 4GB yields 294GB. Neither is a guaranteed purchase threshold. If no past usage log exists, label the small and large growth values as assumptions rather than measurements. Include travel peaks, cleanup habits and budget in the decision.

Before removing originals, use the photo-backup checks. Then compare Pro and Pro Max size and South Korean prices or the total purchase cost. The cleanup planner calculates a free-space target; it does not automatically recommend a device.

Unlocked phone or carrier deal? Compare the full 24-month cost

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-09-26 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

A lower device price can be outweighed by a costly service period or required extras. Compare the same period and the full device principal, then keep conditional benefits separate from confirmed discounts.

Worked example, not an offer.

The A and B quotes below are hypothetical Korean-won inputs, not a current promotion, subsidy or lowest-price claim. They do not establish eligibility, legal discount rules or another country’s pricing.

Define “total” before comparing

Use the same number of service months for both quotes. Include the full device principal, combining upfront and remaining principal. Do not subtract a subsidy twice if it is already reflected. A 36-month installment schedule does not make the remaining principal disappear from a 24-month ownership comparison.

This model adds the full device principal to service costs during the selected period. It is not a cash-flow schedule of payments leaving your bank during those months. Add interest and fees separately and consult the actual payment terms and final contract.

Hypothetical 24-month comparison · KRW
ItemA: unlocked assumptionB: carrier assumption
Full device principal1,990,0001,590,000
Monthly service, first 6 months25,00090,000
Monthly service, next 18 months25,00055,000
Add-ons and coverage over 24 months0120,000
Fees and one-off costs0100,000
Total before resale2,590,0003,340,000
Estimated old-phone proceeds400,000400,000
Net after estimated resale2,190,0002,940,000

B’s service cost is 90,000 × 6 + 55,000 × 18 = KRW 1,530,000; A’s is 25,000 × 24 = KRW 600,000. B saves KRW 400,000 on the device but adds KRW 930,000 in service, KRW 120,000 in extras and KRW 100,000 in other costs. Its net is therefore KRW 750,000 higher.

A’s average net is KRW 91,250 per month. That is not the actual monthly bill: an upfront device payment and delayed resale have different cash timing. Load the example and replace it with your own quotes. For another currency, compare both quotes in the same unit; do not mix currencies or use these examples as exchange-rate guidance.

Ask for five separate categories

  1. Final principal: upfront plus installment principal, after confirmed discounts. Do not add device installments again inside service.
  2. Pure service charges by period: initial months, later months and conditions for changing the plan.
  3. Extras: insurance, add-ons, SIM, shipping, interest and other fees. For varying extras, calculate their period totals first.
  4. Exit conditions: model early cancellation or plan changes separately. Do not assert future penalties are zero.
  5. Trade-in and card benefits: identify whether they were already deducted, when they are paid and what spending or retention conditions apply.

What changes the conclusion?

A KRW 10,000 monthly difference moves a 24-month comparison by KRW 240,000. Reducing B’s first six months by KRW 20,000 saves KRW 120,000. Changing equal resale assumptions on both sides changes your expenditure but not the gap.

The KRW 750,000 gap equals KRW 31,250 per month over 24 months. Holding everything else constant, B needs that much additional net benefit unique to B to break even. A “maximum benefit” is not confirmed money. Check eligibility, duration, extra spending and payment timing; do not count an already-applied device discount twice.

Equal price is not equal service

Compare data allowances, speed caps, tethering, roaming, bundle benefits and support. An inadequate plan can create additional purchases. The calculator covers two service-rate periods and fixed monthly extras, not every complicated contract, conditional card benefit or old-device installment. Run a confirmed-input comparison separately from a conditional-benefit scenario.

item.title: Clicked a suspicious text-message link? Respond to what you actually did
item.description:
Smishing response

Clicked a suspicious text-message link? Respond to what you actually did

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-08-23 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

After a suspicious delivery, penalty or payment text, the next action depends on what happened after the click. Viewing a page, submitting a code, installing an app and making a payment require different responses.

Money moving now?

Contact the relevant bank, card issuer or mobile provider through its verified official channel promptly. In South Korea, the original guide also directs financial-loss reports to police at 112. The numbers in this article are South Korean contacts, not worldwide reporting numbers. Outside South Korea, use the appropriate local official channels.

Stop further interaction and preserve evidence

Do not call the number in the suspicious text, install its “cancellation” app or provide another verification code. Record the message, sender, URL, screen, installed app name and transaction notice where safe. Redact identity details, account numbers and codes before sharing evidence. Do not erase everything before recording the sequence.

What you didFirst actionNext check
Opened the link onlyClose the page and inspect downloads and recent appsUpdates, Play Protect and unusual account alerts
Entered a password or verification codeProtect the affected account from a trusted deviceSessions, recovery information and reused passwords
Installed an app or granted powerful permissionsStop running it and disconnect the suspect phoneOfficial app checks and device support
A transfer, card or carrier-billed payment occurredContact the financial provider and relevant authoritiesPreserve the original message and transaction records

If you only opened the page

Check whether anything was downloaded, installed or submitted. On Android, inspect recently installed apps and unfamiliar APK downloads without executing them. Revoke an unwanted site-notification permission if you granted it. Keep the operating system and browser updated and use Google Play Protect. Monitor unexpected logins, unsolicited codes and billing records. A click alone is not a reason to immediately factory-reset a phone, but it is not proof that nothing else happened either.

If you entered account information

Open the official app or type a verified address from a trusted device. Change the affected password and any reused versions on other services. Review signed-in devices, recent activity, recovery email and phone, and two-step verification. If you supplied a verification code, also inspect connected apps, payment methods and email-forwarding settings; do not assume changing the password addresses every form of access.

If an app or powerful permission was involved

Stop using the app and turn off mobile data and Wi-Fi on the suspected device. Protect important accounts from another trusted device. Review Android’s recent apps, accessibility, device-admin, notification-access and display-over-other-apps permissions with official guidance. If removal fails, permissions return or behavior continues, seek manufacturer or carrier assistance. Consider an official reset only with appropriate support and carefully preserved data; restoring every previous app can restore the unwanted app too.

If money or payment details were involved

Explain whether the event was a bank transfer, card payment or carrier-billed purchase; these have different support channels. Use the card’s printed contact or the official app, not a search advertisement or number from the suspect message. Ask about the provider’s available blocking and dispute procedures. Deleting a text does not reverse a transaction. Keep reference numbers and the time of each report.

South Korean reporting information

The source edition checked KISA’s 118 consultation service, police financial-loss reporting at 112, and the integrated telecommunications-financial-fraud contact 1566-1188. The linked Korean public-agency pages explain their scopes. These contacts were last checked on August 23, 2026; verify the official procedure before relying on them. They are not substitutes for another country’s reporting arrangements.

Prevent secondary harm

If contacts may have been exposed, warn close contacts about unexpected links or money requests using your name. Describe the message without forwarding the suspicious link. Ask the relevant carrier or financial institution about applicable protection and credential-reissue procedures. Do not give remote-control access or codes to someone promising recovery.

item.title: Saving passwords in your browser: personal and shared-device rules
item.description:
Account security

Saving passwords in your browser: personal and shared-device rules

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-14 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Browser password storage can make unique, long passwords practical. Its suitability depends on the device, the operating-system account and the protection around both—not just convenience.

Use it on a device you control

Chrome, Edge and Safari can store credentials and fill them on later visits. On a personal, locked device, this can help avoid reusing one short password everywhere. It does not remove the need for two-step verification, current recovery information and attention to the login address.

EnvironmentPractical ruleAdditional check
Personal device with a screen lockConsider password storageUse unique passwords and two-step verification
Shared family computerUse separate operating-system accountsDo not store private credentials in a shared account
Library, hotel or other public computerDo not save credentialsSign out and check what remains after use

Review what is already saved

Open the browser’s password manager and inspect the site list. Remove obsolete credentials carefully, ensuring that you still have the access information you need. Review unfamiliar entries rather than assuming that a long list is harmless. Menu placement varies by browser version.

Protect the device itself

Use the device’s login password, PIN or supported biometric lock. On a phone without a screen lock or a computer left signed in, another person may have access to browser sessions and credentials. Locking the device is a separate layer from protecting each online account.

A saved password is not a signed-in session

A website may keep you signed in even when the browser did not save its password. Conversely, saving a password does not mean that you remain signed in after logging out. On a shared device, declining the save prompt is not enough: sign out of the website and the browser account as appropriate.

Choose one main storage workflow

Built-in managers are easy to start with and may synchronize through a browser account. A dedicated manager may suit people using several browsers or devices. Review the actual service’s security and recovery options. Whichever you choose, use different passwords for different sites, protect important accounts with two-step verification and avoid public-device storage.

If credentials were left on a public device

From a trusted device, change the affected password and review signed-in devices and account activity. Remove suspicious sessions and review recovery details. Delete the stored credentials from the old computer if you can, but do not rely on deletion alone: someone may already have used or copied them. Password changes and session controls have different effects depending on the service.

item.title: Cloud storage full? Calculate the space you need before deleting
item.description:
Phone replacement · Storage

Cloud storage full? Calculate the space you need before deleting

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-14 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Freeing several gigabytes on a phone may not change a cloud-account warning. Identify the full location first, then account for the next upload and the space you want to retain. This guide concerns personal Google and iCloud accounts, not every business-account or OneDrive rule.

Device storage and cloud capacity are separate

Full locationInspect firstWhat another cleanup does not do
The phone itselfApps, photos and downloads in device settingsA larger cloud plan does not add the same amount of device space
Google AccountPhotos, Drive, Gmail and account usageDeleting device-only copies does not necessarily reduce account usage
iCloudPhotos, backups, Drive and account usageClearing an iPhone app’s cache addresses a different location

When the same item appears on the device and in the cloud, determine which copy an action removes. Ordinary deletion and a device-space feature are not equivalent. See the photo-storage comparison.

Inspect the account’s full usage

Google’s personal-account storage is shared across services, so inspect Gmail and Drive as well as Photos. A full account can affect uploads, email and photo backup. Work and school accounts may have different allocations or policies. Apple distinguishes iCloud storage from device storage and provides usage categories for photos, backups and documents. Do not delete an old backup just because its name is old; decide whether it may still be needed.

Add upcoming uploads and your chosen reserve

This is KYD’s planning formula, not a billing calculation or an automatic cleanup feature. Reserve space is your target, not a mandatory provider percentage.

Required cleanup = max(0, current usage + planned uploads + target reserve − account limit)

Hypothetical example: limit 15GB, usage 14.2GB, incoming photos and videos 2GB, desired reserve 1GB. The calculation is 14.2 + 2 + 1 − 15 = 2.2GB. Making room only for the upload requires 1.2GB; including the chosen reserve requires 2.2GB. These are not measurements from the owner’s account.

Hypothetical candidateAssumed spaceDecision
Photos that appear duplicated but lack verified originals2.5GBDo not prioritize deletion merely because they are large
Unneeded files with separately saved, opened copies1GBReview deletion scope before cleanup
Items with no remaining retention need1.2GBConfirm contents and scope

The illustrative 1GB + 1.2GB matches the 2.2GB target. Actual recovered capacity can differ by service and processing state. Record size rather than only item count: one video can account for substantial space.

Copying inside the same sync library may not be independent

Export or copy required originals to another location and open them. Another copy inside the same cloud account may also consume that account’s storage. An external device is useful but still has loss and failure risks. Emptying trash or deleting a backup can be difficult to reverse; check the service’s actual recovery rules rather than assuming a grace period always exists.

For shared or work material, review ownership and collaboration effects before deleting. If reported usage does not change immediately, do not repeat large deletions blindly.

Keep a local before-and-after record

Location / account: __________
Limit / usage / incoming upload / reserve: __________
Items to preserve: __________
Reported usage before → after: __________
Result of reopening the independent copy: __________

Review the next upload as well as the space just freed. For device capacity, use the phone storage guide; for uncertain originals, use the backup self-check; for a new phone, use the capacity planner.

item.title: Before selling your phone: verify the new device, accounts and eSIM
item.description:
Phone replacement · Selling

Before selling your phone: verify the new device, accounts and eSIM

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-14 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Prepare the new phone before erasing the old one. Photos appearing on the new device do not prove that authenticator apps, payment services and the phone line are ready for handover.

List what must keep working

Include photos, contacts, messenger history, authenticator tools, financial apps and transport or payment services. Transfer methods can differ. “Full backup complete” does not mean that every app has completed its migration.

Illustrative situation: photos appear on the new phone, but an important login still needs a code from the old device. Pause and inspect that service’s official transfer or recovery process before searching for the erase button. This is a hypothetical case, not a reproduced incident or a tested app review.

Give every stage a stop condition

StageVerify yourselfStop when
1. CopiesOpen important photos and files on the new device or separate copyThe only originals remain on the old phone
2. Account accessImportant app logins and recovery methods workAccess depends on an unavailable old-device code
3. Phone lineCalls, texts and SIM or eSIM migration on the new deviceYou cannot receive required calls or verification texts
4. Manufacturer procedureModel-specific account and erase instructionsManagement, loss protection or password issues remain
5. HandoverSetup screen, physical cards and external storageOwner authentication is still required or private files remain

Line transfer and eSIM reissue depend on the carrier and device. Apple distinguishes deleting an eSIM, obtaining a new eSIM and cancelling a plan. Contact the carrier for the latter two as applicable. Verify the new line first; this article does not cancel a subscription or transfer its ownership.

Follow the correct iPhone or Android procedure

iPhone: Apple’s sale or trade-in guidance begins with backup and transfer, then removal of personal information. Review Apple Watch unpairing if relevant. Deleting photos or contacts one by one while signed into iCloud can affect synchronized data. Sign-out options vary by iOS version; follow the current document for your version and its official erase procedure, rather than treating this short summary as every screen.

Android: Google’s reset guidance explains that device data is erased and account-security information may be needed for restoration. Verify access from another device and inspect the official waiting guidance if the Google Account password was recently changed. Manufacturer-specific menus and account-removal steps take priority for your model.

This is for an owner preparing their own device. It does not bypass another owner’s lock or a school or employer’s management controls. Do not solve a lock problem by giving the buyer your account password.

Document the handover without publishing identifiers

Record the condition and setup screen where useful. Keep full serial numbers, IMEI, phone numbers, account addresses and unlock codes out of public sale photographs or reports. Follow the transaction service’s process for any required private information.

New device: important files / logins / calls and texts
Old device: official procedure / setup screen
Separate checks: physical SIM / external memory / connected devices
Remaining issue: __________
Resolved before handover: __________

A setup screen does not automatically prove that every account lock or management policy has been removed. If the buyer’s setup needs previous-owner authentication, resolve it through the manufacturer’s normal process before completing handover.

When this sequence is not enough

  • For a lost device, use the manufacturer’s lost-device guidance; the objective differs from resale.
  • For a broken screen, do not assume backup or sign-out is complete. Seek official support.
  • For a work or school device, obtain the required management approval first.

item.title: Unwanted Android ad notifications: find the sending app first
item.description:
Phone maintenance

Unwanted Android ad notifications: find the sending app first

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-13 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Unexpected ad notifications can come from a website permission or a recently installed app. The first useful clue is the app that sent the notification—not a guess that the entire phone is infected.

Identify the sender without opening the ad

Press and hold the notification to inspect the sending app and its controls. If it is Chrome or Samsung Internet, review that browser’s site-notification permissions. If it is another app, inspect that app’s notification settings and purpose. Tapping the ad itself may take you to another promotion or permission request.

Review browser site permissions

In Chrome, look under Settings, Site settings and Notifications. Block unfamiliar sites that you do not want to hear from. Granting permission while visiting a news, video or download page can allow later notifications even when the page is no longer open. Removing that permission is different from deleting your photos or resetting the phone.

Review recently installed apps

Compare when the unwanted notifications began with recent installations. Simple flashlight, wallpaper or cleanup apps may contain advertising. Remove an unnecessary app using normal settings; for an app you need, first check whether promotional notification categories can be turned off separately. Back up required app data before removal.

SymptomFirst checkCaution
Ads appear after the browser closesBrowser site-notification permissionsConfirm the sender by holding the notification
Full-screen ads begin after opening one appRecent apps and display-over-other-apps permissionKeep needed app data before uninstalling
An alert claims to be a system update or delivery messageOpen the official app independentlyDo not enter passwords or payment details through the alert

Keep important notification channels

Android’s app settings let you adjust notifications, although names vary by manufacturer and version. Where possible, disable the promotional category instead of every notification. Completely silencing a bank or messaging app can hide information you actually need.

Do not add unknown security utilities

Start with the sender, site permissions and installed apps. Installing several unfamiliar security or cleanup apps can create more notifications and more permissions to review. Do not open unexpected APK files in the downloads folder. A factory reset is not an appropriate first diagnostic step for one unwanted notification.

Observe the result and protect privacy

Record whether new notifications still come from the same sender after changing permissions. A notification already displayed does not necessarily establish that the change failed. When helping a family member or student, ask them to show the unwanted alert; you do not need to read their private messages, photos or passwords.

Avoid granting permission just to continue

Be wary of pages that demand notifications to play a video, download a file or claim a coupon. Review requested permissions against an app’s actual purpose before installation. If ads increased after a new app, that timing is a starting point for investigation, not proof that every app in that category is harmful.

Free software installers: read the checkboxes before clicking Next

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-13 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

The program you want may share an installer with optional apps or browser changes. Read each option before accepting it rather than treating every Next button as a neutral step.

Look for Custom or Advanced installation

A quick or recommended setup can include preselected offers. Where an installer provides Custom or Advanced options, inspect the component list. Distinguish a genuine dependency from an unrelated search helper, shopping extension or additional application. An unfamiliar component deserves investigation, not automatic consent.

Check what the permission actually changes

Look for wording about partner services, browser protection, search improvements, the start page or default search engine. Such wording is not automatically proof of malware, but it may authorize something unrelated to the feature you wanted. Uncheck unwanted optional components and read small-print choices before moving on.

Only a prominent quick-install option is visibleLook for custom or advanced optionsOptional offers may be preselected
The installer requests a new browser start pageDecline an unwanted changeIt may not be required for the main program

Use the developer’s own distribution

Prefer a verified official website to a search advertisement or third-party download library. Compare the developer, filename and version: installers for the same program can be packaged differently by different sites. A signature or a trusted-looking site alone is not a blanket safety guarantee.

Inspect the device after installation

Open the installed-apps list in Windows Settings or Control Panel and compare installation dates. Check startup applications, browser extensions, desktop shortcuts, the start page and default search engine. An unfamiliar app installed at the same time is a useful clue, but investigate its purpose before removing a needed component.

Undo unwanted changes

Remove unwanted applications and extensions using the normal controls, restore browser preferences and restart if appropriate. Then observe whether the same symptoms return. If pop-ups or settings changes persist, use official security support rather than installing another unknown repair utility. On managed work or school devices, consult the administrator.

Consent can include settings and agreements

A selected checkbox can authorize both installation and configuration changes. Read the publisher and function of each item, not just the name of the main program. Windows protections against potentially unwanted applications are another layer; they do not replace checking the installer yourself.

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-13 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

A useful error screenshot may also reveal account names, browser tabs, locations or access codes. Review the entire image—not just the message you intended to show.

Crop to the information needed

If support only needs an error message and one menu, capture or crop that area. Inspect the address bar, profile icon, tab titles, bookmarks, notifications, document owner and surrounding conversation. Small details at the edges can identify a person or organization.

Redact more than the obvious name

Check email addresses, phone numbers, account IDs, postal addresses, school names, student records, order and reservation numbers. Partial details can combine with other visible clues. In map and delivery screens, nearby street names, landmarks and a live-location marker can reveal a place even when the full address is covered.

Screenshot typeWhat to preserveWhat to remove or check
Error reportError text and necessary controlsNames, email, account IDs and unrelated tabs
Map or delivery screenOnly the relevant non-sensitive detailAddress, live location and separate file metadata
Payment, ticket or barcodeAvoid sharing the code where possibleBalances, order references and authentication information

Treat QR codes and barcodes as data

They may represent payment, reservations, tickets or login tokens. They are not harmless decorations just because the encoded information is not readable at a glance. Do not post a usable code while covering only the text beside it.

Use an opaque cover or a tighter crop

Light marker strokes, translucent shapes and weak blur may leave readable or inferable content. For sensitive details, remove the area or cover it fully with a solid opaque block. This still requires inspecting the output; an editing overlay is not necessarily a permanent redaction in every format.

Reopen the final export

Save a separate sharing copy and open that exported file in another view. Zoom in to inspect text and codes. Check that it is not a reversible layered project or the untouched original. Review the filename too: it may contain a person’s name or order reference.

Check every image in a set

Redacting the first screenshot does not protect later images. Inspect each file before attaching it and keep the sharing copies clearly separate from the originals. For sensitive records, follow the organization’s disclosure rules rather than assuming any edited screenshot is suitable for public posting.

item.title: Website changes not showing? Check the response before clearing data
item.description:
Browser troubleshooting

Website changes not showing? Check the response before clearing data

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

An old-looking page is not automatically a cache problem. Compare the URL, deployed HTML and stylesheet first so that you do not erase logins or offline work unnecessarily.

Start with one URL and one visible change

Copy the complete address, including the host and path. A www address, a different signed-in account or a different language setting can legitimately show another page. Choose one changed sentence or button label as the evidence to compare, rather than relying on an impression that the design looks different.

ObservationNext checkWhat it does not prove
Only the normal window looks oldCache, extensions, signed-in content and service workersA private-window difference alone does not prove caching
Another device also gets the old sentenceProduction commit, output folder and domain targetWhether both requests passed through the same CDN cache
Text is new, spacing or colors are oldThe CSS URL and its actual responseWhether caching or selector priority is responsible
Only the preview URL is newProduction branch and domain deploymentThat a successful preview reached production

Reloading is different from deleting data

In Chrome or Edge on Windows, try a normal reload and then Ctrl + Shift + R. A private window provides another comparison, but changes account and extension conditions; it does not clear the server or CDN cache. If clearing cached images and files is necessary, inspect the selected boxes. Cookies, site data and saved passwords are separate categories. Export or save offline drafts before deleting a web app’s site data.

For site owners: inspect Network responses

  1. Open the browser’s developer tools, select Network and reload.
  2. Record the document’s Request URL and status, including its final redirected address.
  3. Search the Response for your changed sentence. If the response is new but the screen is old, inspect client rendering, service workers and account-specific state.
  4. Inspect the stylesheet separately: compare its URL and content with the deployed CSS.
  5. While developer tools remain open, use Disable cache for a controlled comparison, then restore the setting.

A 304 Not Modified response permits reuse after validation; it is not proof of an error or an outdated file. A 200 response is not proof that the latest commit was served either. Compare content as well as status.

KYD’s documented duplicate-path case

On September 6, 2026, both / and /public/ returned 200 with the same homepage title. /public/posts/windows-file-extension/ also exposed the original article. The repository maintained deployment files in both the root and public folders, so publishing the root exposed two paths. Clearing browser data could not fix this duplication: the correction was a deployed redirect from /public/* to the equivalent canonical path. See the Cloudflare Pages domain and duplicate-path guide.

CSS versions are useful, not magic

A content-hashed filename such as style.a1b2.css is an illustrative way to make new HTML request a new stylesheet. You must update the HTML reference too. Adding ?v=2 depends on the server or CDN cache-key configuration and is not a guaranteed bypass. Before a CDN purge, review the affected URL scope in the service’s official dashboard.

What counts as resolution?

Record the intended sentence and stylesheet from the production domain, then compare a fresh browser session. When requesting help, provide the full URL, check time, expected and actual text, and deployment commit. Do not publish raw network logs that may contain login cookies.

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

A download warning does not establish that a file is malicious, but it is not something to bypass on the strength of a familiar filename. Check what you asked for and where the file actually came from.

Confirm the source independently

Find the developer’s official site through a route you trust, rather than a sponsored search result, blog attachment or unexpected message. Match the publisher, filename and version. A program name can be reused by another distribution site or by a modified installer. If you cannot verify the source, stop rather than opening the file to see what happens.

Show the complete extension

A file described as a document or image may actually end in .exe, .msi, .bat or .scr. If you were not expecting to install software, that mismatch is a reason to cancel. A ZIP archive does not make its contents safe. A separately supplied archive password can also prevent some automated inspection; verify an expected sender through another channel before considering the attachment.

An official-looking download is marked uncommonRecheck the domain, publisher and filenameAsk the supplier if you remain unsure
An unexpected password-protected archive arrivesQuestion the source and purposeA password is not evidence of safety
Instructions tell you to disable warningsStop the downloadDisabling protection does not verify the file

Read the specific warning

Chrome distinguishes different warning reasons, including uncommon downloads and dangerous files. Do not assume that every message means the same thing. A false positive is possible, but you cannot establish safety merely by dismissing a dialog. Popularity, an official-looking page or a security scan on its own is not a guarantee.

Before running a needed installer

Check file properties and available publisher information, and use the device’s security checks. On a work or school computer, ask the administrator rather than overriding policy. Consider whether you actually need the program: vague promises to speed up a device, repair every error or provide free coupons are not a reason to run unfamiliar software.

If you already ran it

Inspect newly installed apps, browser extensions, the start page and default search engine. Remove unwanted additions through the normal settings and review account activity if you entered credentials. Do not treat removal as proof that every possible effect has been reversed. Escalate to the device administrator or official support if suspicious behavior continues.

Reduce future mistakes

Keep unknown installers out of the downloads folder so that they are not executed later by accident. For a shared family computer, a standard user account adds a separate approval step for installations. It does not turn an unsafe program into a safe one. item.description:

Cloudflare Pages domain still pending? Check DNS and certificates separately

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

A pending domain can involve DNS delegation, the Pages custom-domain association or certificate validation. Identify which stage is incomplete instead of repeatedly deleting and recreating the same settings.

Verify nameserver delegation where required

For a Cloudflare-managed zone, compare the nameservers configured at the registrar with the exact pair assigned by Cloudflare. Old or misspelled entries can prevent the expected delegation. Nameserver requirements differ for a root domain and a subdomain using an external DNS provider; use the official custom-domain instructions for your setup rather than applying one method to every host.

Add the domain inside the Pages project

Creating a DNS record is not the same as registering a custom domain with Pages. Inspect the project’s Custom domains screen and its validation status. Compare the target with the intended production deployment. A working pages.dev URL helps distinguish a file-deployment problem from a custom-domain problem; it does not establish that DNS and HTTPS are ready.

ObservationCheckAvoid
Nameservers still point to the previous providerRegistrar delegation and Cloudflare’s assigned pairRepeated changes during propagation
A DNS record exists but Pages has no custom domainThe project’s Custom domains setupAssuming a manual CNAME completes association
DNS resolves but HTTPS failsCertificate status, validation messages and CAA recordsChanging proxy and redirect settings at random

Root and www are different hosts

kyd.kr and www.kyd.kr require separate checks. If both are used, configure the appropriate associations and choose one canonical destination. One can be active while the other remains pending. Test the already-active address before changing it to troubleshoot the other.

Check DNSSEC and record conflicts

If the setup remains pending, compare DNS records and dashboard errors. When changing DNS providers, stale DNSSEC delegation information, including a registrar’s DS record, can cause validation failures. Review the provider’s instructions before altering security settings. Preserve mail and unrelated service records; changing nameservers is not permission to delete them.

Waiting is a checkpoint, not a diagnosis

DNS caches and certificate issuance can take time. A short wait immediately after a change is not by itself proof of failure. The original guide used a next-day check as a practical reminder, not a guaranteed 24-hour completion deadline. Record what changed and inspect current DNS responses and certificate errors instead of restarting configuration repeatedly.

Prepare useful support evidence

Provide the hostname, registrar delegation, expected DNS target, Pages status, check time and exact error. Keep account IDs and API tokens out of screenshots. If files work on pages.dev but not on the custom domain, say so; that narrows the investigation without claiming that every Pages setting is correct.

item.title: Cloudflare Pages custom domains: verify deployment and duplicate URLs
item.description:
Website operations

Cloudflare Pages custom domains: verify deployment and duplicate URLs

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

A connected-domain badge does not prove that every path serves the intended file. Separate the registrar, DNS, Pages project and deployment output, then test actual responses.

Four responsibilities, not one

The registrar manages domain ownership and renewal. Authoritative DNS directs hostnames. The Pages project chooses the repository, branch and build output to publish. The deployed files supply the content. Gabia was a registrar example in the original guide, not a verified claim about KYD’s registrar.

  1. Confirm the intended page works at the Pages deployment URL before investigating the domain.
  2. Add each intended hostname under the project’s Custom domains.
  3. Follow Cloudflare’s conditions for root domains or subdomains using external DNS.
  4. Preserve email and other service records before changing delegation.
  5. Once association and certificates are ready, test HTTPS and the canonical destination with real requests.

KYD’s actual duplicate-path observation

Before correction on September 6, 2026, the following paths returned duplicate content. These are observations of public HTTP responses, not a review of every Cloudflare setting or another project’s configuration.

PathBefore correctionIntended behavior
/Homepage, 200Canonical homepage
/public/The same homepage, 200Permanent redirect to /
/posts/windows-file-extension/Article, 200Canonical article
/public/posts/windows-file-extension/The same article, 200Permanent redirect without /public

After deployment on September 7, /public/ returned 301 to /, and the duplicate article returned 301 to its equivalent /posts/ path. Both destinations returned 200. /blog redirected to /posts/ with 301, while an arbitrary missing path returned 404. Comparing the same paths before and after established that those rules were actually applied.

Publish redirects in the deployment output

The repository held equivalent files in the root and public folders. Publishing the root could expose public as a second web path. Choose the intended output folder and address any already-public duplicates. For this static Pages case, the deployed _redirects file included:

/public / 301
/public/* /:splat 301

The wildcard preserves each article’s remaining path rather than sending everything to the homepage. A generic local HTTP server does not execute Cloudflare’s redirect rules. Routes handled by Pages Functions may need separate handling; review the official scope.

Check six things after connecting

  • HTTP redirects to the intended HTTPS address.
  • Root and www converge on one canonical host.
  • Article URLs work directly and after a reload.
  • Missing pages return an actual 404, not just an error-looking page with 200.
  • robots.txt, sitemap.xml and verification files are not replaced with homepage HTML.
  • Folder prefixes and old URLs resolve consistently with the canonical tag.

A canonical tag is a preferred-URL signal; a 301 moves a request. Adding the tag does not remove duplicate public paths.

When a new deployment looks old

Compare the GitHub commit, production deployment commit and changed sentence in the public HTML. Do not repeatedly change DNS before checking deployment status. The response and cache guide explains how to distinguish these causes.

item.description:

Email attachments: seven checks before you open a file

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

An invoice, meeting document or school notice can look routine while carrying an unexpected file or a phishing link. Check the context and requested action as well as the displayed sender name.

Seven checks, in order

  1. Actual sender address: expand the sender details and inspect the complete domain. A display name is not proof of identity.
  2. Expected context: were you waiting for this file, and does the wording match the conversation? A familiar account can itself be compromised.
  3. Complete extension: show extensions in Windows. Unexpected .exe, .js, .bat or .scr files are not ordinary documents.
  4. Archive contents: inspect filenames before running anything. Nested or password-protected archives deserve additional verification.
  5. Login destination: if a document redirects to a login screen, verify its address independently before entering credentials.
  6. Urgency and payment demands: an account suspension or immediate invoice deadline is a reason to pause, not skip checks.
  7. Independent confirmation: use a known phone number, established messenger conversation or official contact channel—not just a reply to the suspicious message.
SituationNext actionImportant limit
An expected person sends an expected fileRecheck the address, format and contextA familiar sender account can be compromised
A message demands urgent payment or loginOpen the official app or saved address independentlyDo not use the attached file to verify itself
A macro document, executable or encrypted archive arrivesTreat it as higher risk and verify through another channelA password-protected archive is not safer by default

Why ordinary-looking messages deserve care

Attackers can use familiar labels such as quotation, payroll, receipt, shipping notice or meeting material. Evaluate the sender, format, tone and action together. A file’s friendly name does not establish what it does when opened.

What to do if uncertain

Leave the file unopened and contact the expected sender through a channel you already know. Open any required service through its official app or a verified address. Chrome and Gmail warnings are additional signals; disabling them does not establish authenticity.

If you already opened it

Record whether you merely viewed a file, enabled a feature, installed software or entered credentials. Check for unwanted apps, browser changes and unfamiliar account activity. Protect affected accounts from a trusted device and review two-step verification. For a managed device, report to the responsible team rather than attempting an unverified cleanup yourself.

Keep organizational rules simple

Agree on a small set of memorable rules: do not run unexpected executables from email, independently verify password-protected archives, and revisit login requests through known official addresses. Make the reporting contact clear so that a suspicious attachment is reported without being forwarded broadly or opened for demonstration.

A Google Account can connect email, Drive, Photos, calendars and phone backups. Protecting it involves recovery access and active sessions as well as a unique password.

Start with the account’s security screen

Open the official Google Account controls directly and review recent security activity and signed-in devices. An unfamiliar device, a message you did not send or an unexpected recovery change deserves investigation. Device labels and locations are clues, not an automatic diagnosis by themselves.

SituationFirst actionDo not stop at
An unfamiliar login alertReview recent activity and signed-in devicesChanging a password without reviewing sessions
Old recovery phone or emailUpdate to information you can accessLeaving another person’s contact as a temporary solution
The same password is used elsewhereCreate a unique password for each servicePassword uniqueness without two-step verification

Keep recovery information usable

Check that the recovery email and phone number are yours and still accessible. An old number or an abandoned mailbox may complicate recovery when you need it most. When helping someone else, let the account owner enter their own information and credentials; do not make yourself the default holder of their recovery access.

Add two-step verification and a fallback

Review the methods supported by the account, such as prompts, authenticator tools or security keys. Enable a suitable method and keep backup codes in a protected location that remains available if the phone is lost. A second factor reduces risk but does not make every login request legitimate.

Review connected apps

Inspect third-party services granted account access and remove those you no longer use. Review app passwords where applicable. An old integration may continue to have permissions even if you stopped visiting its website. Consider the required function and the actual permission scope.

Use a unique account password

If the same password appears on several sites, one breach can threaten other accounts. A password manager can make separate long passwords manageable. Protect its own access and recovery path too.

If you suspect account takeover

Review suspicious sessions, recovery information and connected apps as well as changing the password from a trusted device. A password-only response can leave overlooked permissions or recovery changes. Follow Google’s account-security guidance for the specific situation. Do not share passwords, verification codes or screenshots containing recovery information while asking for help.

A routine that respects privacy

Review these settings after changing devices or contact details and when account alerts appear. For family or student support, explain the screen and let the owner operate it. Helping with security does not require reading their messages or keeping their password.

Before sending a Drive link, decide who should access the file and what they should be able to do. A link’s convenience can conceal a broader sharing scope than you intended.

Restricted and anyone with the link are different

Restricted sharing grants access to authorized people rather than everyone who receives a link. Anyone-with-the-link access can extend beyond the original message because the link can be forwarded. For personal information, internal records or sensitive school and work documents, start with the narrowest appropriate scope.

Match the role to the task

A viewer reads the file; a commenter can leave feedback; an editor can change content. Distribution alone often needs only viewing. Give editing access only to people who actually need to collaborate. Available permissions and organizational restrictions depend on the file and account.

Collaborate on editingEditor access only for required participantsReview capabilities such as moving, deleting or resharing

Inspect the file before sharing

Look for names, phone numbers, email addresses, student records, addresses or evaluations. Decide whether each recipient needs that information. Then inspect general access and the people list. Do not infer permissions from the message in which the link will be sent.

Watch folder inheritance

Folder permissions can affect files inside it. If one document needs a narrower audience, review inherited access and consider a separate restricted location. Do not assume changing one visible setting overrides every inherited or organizational rule.

Review access after sending

Check that the intended recipient can open the file and that an unintended account cannot. A private-window test can help inspect general link access, but it does not simulate every organizational role. When distributing a copy, inspect the original and copy separately: their sharing states may differ.

Close temporary access

At the end of a project, event or term, remove unnecessary external accounts, reduce excess editor roles and disable public link access where no longer needed. A periodic review of important folders helps uncover old links. Follow organizational retention and external-sharing rules before moving, copying or deleting records.

Changing permissions is not recalling copies

Test the access experience after a change and update links in related documents or boards if necessary. Restricting the original does not undo information that someone already downloaded or copied. Choose the audience carefully before the first share, not just at cleanup time.

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Restarting can help, but first find out whether the problem affects one device, one room, one website or the whole connection. That comparison makes the next action more useful.

Compare one thing at a time

Open the same site on another device, then try another site. If only a laptop is slow, inspect its Wi-Fi connection, browser and background updates. If one site is slow everywhere, the site itself may be involved. If all devices struggle, compare the router, modem and provider connection rather than assuming one cause.

Only one device is slowIts Wi-Fi, apps and updatesThat the router has failed
Every device is slowWired access, equipment lights and provider noticesThat a more expensive plan is necessarily needed
A restart helps only brieflyHeat, firmware and connection historyThat repeated resets solve the underlying cause

Separate Wi-Fi coverage from the internet connection

Try the same device closer to the router. Walls, metal furniture and nearby interference can affect wireless coverage. Where available, compare a wired connection. Turning off Wi-Fi and trying mobile data provides another route, but remember that it uses a different network and may incur charges. Record the conditions rather than treating these comparisons as definitive diagnoses.

Look for busy periods

Large downloads, game updates, cloud backups and simultaneous video use can compete for the connection. Note whether the slowdown happens at a particular time or with particular tasks. Inspect active work before assuming hardware failure.

Restart is not factory reset

Follow the equipment manufacturer or provider’s restart procedure. The original guide described switching power off, waiting roughly ten seconds and restarting; separate modem-and-router setups may require the modem to stabilize first. Record the light pattern before and after. A factory reset erases configuration and is a different operation: do not begin with it.

If the problem persists

Review placement and official firmware instructions. Preserve the Wi-Fi name, access details and required connection configuration before making changes. An older router serving many devices may be a limiting factor, but compare wired performance and provider status before purchasing replacement equipment or changing the plan.

Make the support report specific

Provide the affected devices, whether wired access differs, the time pattern, light status and actions already tried. Change one variable, then observe the result. If you change power, position, cabling and settings together, you lose the evidence of which action helped.

item.title: Starting with a password manager without locking yourself out
item.description:
Password management

Starting with a password manager without locking yourself out

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

A password manager makes different passwords for different sites easier to maintain. Start with the vault’s protection and recovery path before moving every account into it.

Understand what changes

Instead of remembering every site password, you protect a vault and use it to store or fill separate credentials. This reduces the practical pressure to reuse one password. It is not a tool that eliminates every risk, and generated passwords can still be exposed through phishing, device compromise or other failures.

Protect the main password and recovery path

Where the manager uses a master password, choose a long, unique passphrase that you do not use on another website. Avoid birthdays, phone numbers and account names. Review the actual manager’s recovery procedure before relying on it. A securely stored offline record may be useful; do not keep the only recovery copy inside the account that could become inaccessible.

StepActionCheck before continuing
Begin migrationStart with three to five important accountsAccess still works after each change
Choose the master passwordUse a long, unique passphraseIt is not reused anywhere else
Prepare recoveryProtect codes and a second access methodThe only copy is not in one cloud account

Move important accounts gradually

Email and cloud accounts often support resets for other services, so start there, then work through financial, shopping and frequently used work accounts. Generate and save a new password, sign out and verify that you can sign in again. Do not change every password in one sitting without checking that the manager saved each one correctly.

Use two-step verification too

Protect the manager itself and important email accounts with a suitable second factor where supported. Keep recovery codes separately and verify access to a backup method. Losing the phone should not mean losing the only route back to every account.

Do not overrule missing autofill blindly

If the manager does not recognize a login page, inspect the complete address. A different domain may be a phishing warning, although missing autofill alone does not prove fraud. Do not manually paste credentials merely because an unexpected page asks you to.

Avoid two conflicting credential lists

If you use both browser storage and a dedicated manager, decide which one is the primary record. Duplicate or outdated entries can make it difficult to know which password is current. Review old entries carefully rather than deleting access information you have not verified elsewhere.

Rehearse the recovery plan safely

Read the emergency instructions and locate the recovery codes, registered email and security key before a real lockout. Check that a second method is actually available if a phone is lost. This is preparation, not a reason to deliberately lock or erase a working account.

Is that PDF link safe? Check the URL, filename and links inside

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

A “view PDF” message presents three separate questions: where the link goes, what file you receive and where links inside the document lead. Passing one check does not settle the next.

Message link → downloaded file → document link

  1. Message link: text such as form.pdf may point somewhere else. On a computer, inspect the hover destination; on a phone, use an address-copy feature if the app provides one. Some previews connect immediately, so use another contact method when the message is suspicious.
  2. Downloaded file: inspect the end of its full name. form.pdf.exe is an executable name with .pdf in the middle. Even an actual .pdf extension does not verify file contents.
  3. Link inside the document: a signature button can lead to a separate site. Check the new destination again if it asks for login, payment or installation.

Read these example URLs without opening them

These are educational strings, not reports of real attacks or clickable destinations. The host identifies the server; a path or query value does not replace it.

Example stringHostWhat remains unknown
https://docs.example.com/form.pdfdocs.example.comThe response format and sender’s authenticity
https://example.com@files.example.org/form.pdffiles.example.orgThe text before @ is not the destination host
https://files.example.org/example.com/form.pdffiles.example.orgThe institution-like text is only in the path
https://files.example.org/?document=form.pdffiles.example.orgA query value ending in .pdf does not guarantee a PDF response

Use the local URL structure checker to compare the hosts without visiting them. An @ in a path or query is different from the user-information separator before the host.

A login request is not automatically fake

Restricted Drive or business documents can legitimately require login. Confirm that you expected the document, recognize the service and have the correct address. Open the service independently or ask the sender to verify the invited account and permissions.

SituationActionDo not assume
An expected document has a permission errorAsk the sender to check your account and roleThat the error itself proves phishing
Viewing requires a new app or certificateStop and confirm through an established official contactThat a logo verifies the installation
The PDF is password protectedConfirm the file and password channel independentlyThat encryption proves either danger or safety
The browser blocks the downloadRequest an official original or alternative documentThat a structural URL check overrides a security warning

If you already acted

Record separately when you saw the message, opened the link, downloaded or executed a file, and entered information. Do not include the password or verification code itself in a report. Follow the action-based response guide. For work documents, use the responsible team instead of uploading confidential files to a public scanning service.

Know the limit of basic checks

A matching host and extension are clues, not malware certification. HTTPS protects a connection; it does not establish the document author’s identity. Do not forward a suspicious file to friends to see whether it opens. The September 6 revision separated these three stages and distinguished normal access controls from warning signs.

Public Wi-Fi: check the network and the destination separately

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

English edition adapted on 2026-10-05. The original source-check date is retained below; this is not a fresh product or match investigation.

Public Wi-Fi is convenient, and HTTPS protects much modern web traffic. Still check the network you join and the website you use: an encrypted connection to an impostor site is not a trusted transaction.

Verify the exact hotspot name

Compare the network name with the venue’s official notice or ask staff. Similar names can belong to different access points. A familiar-looking SSID is not proof of who operates it. If you cannot establish which network is intended, use another connection.

Review auto-join and sharing

Disable automatic connection to public networks you do not need regularly, or forget them after use. On a Windows laptop, use the appropriate public-network profile and inspect network discovery, file sharing and printer sharing. Do not apply Windows menu instructions to every phone platform; controls differ by device.

Task or observationPractical choiceAdditional check
General search or news readingUse the intended site over HTTPSKeep unnecessary sharing and auto-join off
Banking, payment or important account changesPrefer mobile data or another trusted route where practicalVerify the destination and avoid urgent unexpected prompts
Several similar hotspot namesConfirm the exact SSID with the venueDo not select solely by signal strength

Understand what HTTPS does

HTTPS encrypts communication with the selected site and reduces interception risks. It does not make a fake login page genuine, make downloaded software trustworthy or prevent every device problem. Continue checking the domain and browser warnings even on a private network.

Choose the connection to fit the task

For sensitive work, consider using mobile data, a personal hotspot or a connection you control. A trusted VPN may be part of an organization’s policy, but it is not a substitute for verifying websites or files. Do not install an unfamiliar VPN merely because a hotspot advertises it.

Clean up after the session

Disconnect when finished and review saved networks. If you used a shared computer, do not save credentials and sign out of websites and the browser account as appropriate. Public networking and public-device use are separate risks; changing the network does not remove a session from someone else’s computer.

If something seems wrong

Record the actual action and account involved. If you entered a password on an unexpected page, review that account from a trusted device, starting with important email and recovery-linked services. Do not conclude that every account was compromised merely because you used public Wi-Fi.

QR code safety: inspect the address before login or payment

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

A QR code saves typing; it does not certify the link inside it. Inspect the destination and requested action before entering credentials, installing an app or making a payment.

Read the preview before continuing

A phone’s camera or QR app may show the destination before opening it. Compare the domain with the expected service or institution. A shortened address hides the final destination; a long or unfamiliar string alone does not prove fraud, but it should not be accepted without context.

Look for a replacement sticker

On menus, posters, delivery notices and payment signs, check whether another label has been placed over the original code. For payments or logins, confirm the official code with staff or an organizer through a trusted route. Rescanning the same altered code does not correct its destination.

SituationFirst actionStop when
A menu or public noticeInspect the sticker and preview addressA simple notice unexpectedly demands sensitive credentials
An unexpected QR code in a messageConfirm through a known contact or official siteThe sender or purpose remains unverified
A payment screenCheck the amount, business and recipientAny detail differs from what you intended

Verify each new request

A survey, attendance form or menu can become a phishing route if it leads to an unfamiliar login. Inspect the final browser address again. If it asks for an APK, new permissions or an unexpected app installation, pause and verify the official procedure. A recognizable logo is not sufficient evidence.

For QR payments

Before authorizing the transaction, check the recipient and amount on the actual payment confirmation screen. Cancel if either is unexpected and ask the business to confirm. Do not assume that the physical location of a printed code proves who receives the money.

For people distributing QR codes

Print the service name or readable destination beside the code and explain what users should expect. Provide a way to verify it independently. At the end of an event or course, remove outdated notices or clearly manage the destination so that old codes do not become misleading entry points.

Remember the underlying rule

Judge the domain, context and requested information, not the visual pattern of the code. A QR code can carry a valid link or an unwanted one. A preview and structural check can reveal clues, but neither guarantees that a website, file or transaction is safe.

iPhone and Android photo backups: six checks before deleting originals

By KYD Editorial · First published 2026-07-12 · Last editorial review 2026-10-05

“Backup switched on” and “I can reopen the original” are different pieces of evidence. Before deleting photos or changing phones, check the account, upload state, actual files, videos, extra folders and independent copies.

iCloud sync is not two independent photo copies

Apple’s iCloud Photos guidance explains that edits and deletions synchronize across devices using the library. Items in iCloud Photos are not duplicated again in the iCloud device backup. Seeing a photo on two phones signed into the same account therefore does not establish two independent backups.

ActionScopeEvidence to check first
Delete in iCloud PhotosDeletion affects the synchronized libraryDo required originals exist separately?
Google Photos Free up space on AndroidRemoves device copies of backed-up itemsCorrect account, completed backup and actual originals
Ordinary Google Photos deletionDifferent from device-space cleanupRead Google’s deletion guidance
Copy originals outside synchronizationKeeps a copy at another locationDoes the copied file actually open?

After Android’s Free up space operation, items may not be available in the device gallery or offline. Do not assume an iPhone uses the same menu or workflow.

Pair six checks with evidence

Google distinguishes the overall backup state, individual item status and device-folder settings. The following is KYD’s checklist for noticing those differences, not a certification test.

CheckEvidenceIf uncertain
1. AccountThe upload account matches the account viewed elsewhereKeep originals and resolve the account mismatch
2. Upload stateNo pending or paused process; inspect important itemsCheck connectivity and cloud space first
3. Recent originalsOpen recent files on another deviceA thumbnail alone is insufficient
4. VideoInspect playback, sound and durationPreserve the original independently
5. Other foldersCompare messenger, download and editing foldersReview each app’s export and backup scope
6. Independent copyOpen important files copied outside syncPostpone irreversible deletion until a copy is ready

Use the six-item self-check →

The tool does not read or upload photos. It records only what you mark during the page session and does not certify backup success or recovery. Checking samples cannot prove the integrity of every file.

Matching counts do not finish the check

Hypothetical example: a camera folder contains 980 photos and 20 videos, while a messenger folder contains 70 more images. A web library showing 1,000 items does not prove those 70 images were included. A count difference does not establish loss either: compare duplicates, accounts and display scope. These numbers are illustrative, not the owner’s photo count.

The next action is to find important recent and older originals in each folder and open them elsewhere—not delete them. Record a thumbnail and an opened original as different evidence.

Record location and reopening results privately

Download cloud originals or copy device files outside the synchronized library, then open the photo and video files. Review export formats if Live Photos, edits or originals matter. Do not publish account addresses, private images or the backup location to prove that you used this guide.

item.description:
